key_insight: An active-learning MTP-to-FE pipeline can predict heat-transfer trends in FLiBe-based molten salts, enabling rapid screening of coolant composition effects.
engineering_relevance: The workflow links atomistic transport-property prediction to exchanger-scale performance, supporting early-stage design and safety assessment for molten salt reactor coolants.
method: Train moment tensor potentials on ab initio data for FLiBe, FLiBe-LaF3, and FLiBe-UF4.
Run molecular dynamics to extract density, viscosity, thermal conductivity, and heat capacity versus temperature and composition.
Feed the transport properties into a 3D finite-element model of a linear heat exchanger to predict heat-transfer coefficients.
evidence_signal: The FE model using literature properties matched pure FLiBe experiments within 10% in laminar flow and 18% in transitional/turbulent flow, while MTP-MD inputs overestimated heat-transfer coefficient by 25-28%.
watch_item: Predicted absolute performance for the ternary salts depends on MTP accuracy, since transport-property biases propagate directly into the FE heat-transfer results.
paper_title: Integrating moment tensor potentials with finite-element modeling for heat transfer prediction in FLiBe-based molten salt systems
